 EPFO launches WhatsApp service for subscribers to check PF balance and passbook
 The roll out of the scheme coincided with EPFO’s 74th Foundation Day celebration
 By BL New Delhi Bureau 
 Updated - November 01, 2026 at 06:38 PM. 
 | 
 New Delhi
 × Share
 WhatsApp X Facebook LinkedIn Messenger Reddit Mail https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/news/epfo-launches-whatsapp-service-for-subscribers-to-check-pf-balance-and-passbook/article71652835.ece Copy 
 Since-mid September, the EPFO has been carrying out the data transformation and other background logistics upgrades online to offer the WhatsApp channel access scheme
 Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) subscribers can now access their PF balance and passbook through a verified WhatsApp service scheme which was rolled out on Sunday.
 Launched by Union Labour & Employment Minister Mansukh Mandaviya, through the WhatsApp, EPFO members can also see latest five transactions and passbook information, besides receiving personalised guidance and assistance in completing PMVBRY-related requirements which would eliminate physical visits to the offices for routine transactions.
 Since-mid September, the EPFO has been carrying out the data transformation and other background logistics upgrades online to offer the WhatsApp channel access scheme.
 Apart from that, Ministry of Labour & Employment said in a statement that subscribers having Aadhaar-verified inoperative EPF accounts with balances up to ₹1,000 will not be required to file individual claims. EPFO will initiate settlement automatically after prescribed identity and bank-account verification, facilitating transfer of eligible dues to rightful beneficiaries. Approximately one lakh accounts involving ₹5 crore are expected to benefit.
 The roll out of the scheme coincided with EPFO’s 74th Foundation Day celebration.
 Emphasising that social security must be driven by human sensitivity, Mandaviya stressed that every concern and grievance of workers must be addressed with compassion and empathy, viewing each worker with the respect and dignity they deserve as nation-builders. Commending the relentless efforts behind technological transformations like CITES 2.01, he called upon every official to focus on the welfare of the worker at the last mile. He urged officials to take inspiration from the ‘Panch Pran’ articulated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. “ Seva is our sanskaar ,” Mandaviya underlined, and encouraged all to contribute towards accomplishing the goal of Viksit Bharat.
 Worker-centric innovations
 The Minister urged officials to focus on worker-centric innovations across domains in the run-up to EPFO’s 75th year, adapting, building resilience, and evolving processes in tandem with changing times. He also extended Diwali greetings and wished for the light of success and prosperity in the lives of all EPFO officials, members and beneficiaries.
 Chandra Bhushan Kumar, Secretary, Ministry of Labour & Employment, emphasised that social protection and labour reforms must reach not just the organised sector, but unorganised sector workers at the last mile, noting that EPFO sets an example of how to achieve this through institutionalised processes.
 Central Provident Fund Commissioner Ramesh Krishnamurthi, in his address, reflected on EPFO’s 74-year journey, from the founding commitment of 1952 to its present role as a national social security institution serving approximately 8 crore contributory members and 85 lakh pensioners, while safeguarding a retirement corpus of nearly ₹32 lakh crore.
 Highlighting the need to make EPFO more accessible, reliable and humane, he emphasised that institutional trust is built through every claim settled, every pension delivered and every family supported during difficult times.
 The impact of EPFO’s technological transformation through CITES 2.01 was also showcased. A significant improvement in claim settlement was highlighted, with the average settlement time declining to 2.57 days in October 2026. The improvement reflects the organisation’s continuing efforts to make access to provident fund savings faster and more convenient for members, stated the Ministry.
